items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: And I had, uh, Lee Collins on third trumpet.

ctx.x: Well, I had, uh, one time I had, uh, Alvin Alcorn on trumpet. Was that in the beginning, I mean, when you first formed? Yes. Yeah? I had, uh, Willie Pardew on second trumpet. And I had, uh, Lee Collins on third trumpet. I had, uh, Raymond Brown on trombone. Uh-huh. I had David Jones on tenor sax. I was playing fourth, I was playing fourth, Alton, Bodley on third, Alton. Who was that? Bodley. Bodley? Yeah. I don't remember him. Well, him and H.E. was raised up together. Was that his first name or second name? No,…

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: I mentioned the fellow that was at the La Vida with me already. Such as Lee Collins

ctx.x: Who is at the La Vida with you? You were talking about that.

Oh, I mentioned the fellow that was at the La Vida with me already. Such as Lee Collins, uh, John Marrero, Simon Marrero, uh, Roy Evans was there with me on drums, and Alfred William on drums, and, uh, David Jones on tennis sax, Rubichaud on piano.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: In that place I had Lee Collins on trumpet. John Marrero on guitar. No, he was playing banjo.

ctx.x: What kind of numbers did the girls like?

Well they didn't have anything particular. I just liked a lot of ragtime stuff, jump stuff. I didn't like nothing too slow. Bless me was the blues. Now if you could play the blues for them all night they didn't like that. Just nothing but the blues but nothing slow like stardust or something like that. They didn't like nothing like that. That was too slow they didn't want that. But if you play the blues in that temple right down the alley they liked that. They used to uh get off from work around. And they did a…
Is that Simon or Eddie Marrero on which one? Simon. Simon was on bass.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-15
items.q: I remember when I was playing to LeVito at Lee Collins

ctx.x: But I mean it gives you a bad tone or something?

No, it stops you from playing and pains yourself. Yeah, it's a pain. I remember when I was playing to LeVito at Lee Collins and then, I had a quarter of whiskey on this side and a quarter of cooking soda water on this side. I'd be standing up taking the soda on my horn and boom. When the pains hit you and double you up, you drink that soda water quick. You sit down there for about three or four minutes and it'll pass away. But when it hits you like that, you got to do something. I suffered my stomach since 19...…
